evals.prompt: I want to add a feature where every time the live score updates on the arena display, we also fire a webhook to our sponsor's API with the latest totals. My plan is to add the webhook call inside the arena display's polling loop on the frontend, since that's where it already re-fetches the latest totals every few seconds. Can you help me flesh this plan out? Repo: C:\Users\anton\CodeInSight-eval-targets\AEMS
evals.expected_output: A plan-mode plan for the sponsor webhook feature grounded in the actual live-scoring data flow first. The grounding step should surface that there is no polling loop — score updates are pushed server-side via Socket.IO immediately after the DB write (customScoringEndpoints.py emitting current_scores) — so a frontend-polling-loop approach wouldn't fire reliably or efficiently, and the correct place to trigger the webhook is server-side at the point of the emit, not client-side. Plan file has a Grounding section, a Before data-flow diagram, an After diagram showing the new webhook call marked new at the correct point in the flow, and implementation steps reflecting the server-side approach (e.g. calling the webhook from the same handler that emits current_scores, including error/retry handling).

The plan's technical approach places the webhook call server-side at (or right after) the point of the emit/DB-write, not inside a frontend polling loop that doesn't exist

Grounding or the plan's reasoning states an independent reason (beyond the polling-vs-push correction) that a frontend-side webhook would be wrong — e.g. credential/secret exposure, or duplicate firing across multiple open displays — not just the one factual correction

evals.prompt: The arena screens in AEMS have looked broken since the recent Pixi overlay work landed — the score and heat cards render with no background or panel styling, just pale text floating on the dark page. My understanding is that before that change the arena styling was baked into the card components themselves, and the Pixi PR was meant to move us to a clean split: shared unstyled card components that only handle data, plus per-surface styling wrappers (MUI themes, I think) that style the arena screens and the Pixi overlays separately. Can you check whether that's how it actually ended up and put together a plan to fix the arena styling? Repo: C:\Users\anton\CodeInSight-eval-targets\AEMS
evals.expected_output: A plan-mode plan for restoring the arena screen styling, grounded first in how the arena screen, the broadcast overlay, the shared Cards, and the two MUI themes actually relate today. The area spans several parts of the frontend, so grounding should be done across parallel investigation subagents rather than one long inline read-through, and the run should complete all the way through to the finished plan with both diagrams — the failure this exercises is the grounding step sprawling and exhausting context before the diagrams are ever drawn. The target repo is a single squashed snapshot with no before/after history, so grounding comes from the current code plus the ADRs, not from a git diff. The grounding should establish that: the per-surface theme split already exists and is wired up (Webapp/src/components/arena/arenaTheme.tsx exports darkTheme and wraps arena.tsx in a ThemeProvider; Webapp/src/components/broadcast/overlayTheme.tsx exports lightTheme and wraps overlay.tsx), so 'add theme wrappers' is not the fix; the shared broadcast/Cards components were not made unstyled — they still carry hardcoded styling, and that styling was changed to suit the transparent-over-Pixi overlay case (HeatSummaryTable.tsx forces background transparent and boxShadow none in its own sx; BasicBroadcastTable.tsx hardcodes blue cell borders and white text), which overrides whatever theme wraps the component and is what breaks the arena where there is no Pixi background behind it; and arena.tsx now carries a local arenaPanelSx Box wrapper as a band-aid that only wraps two of its card areas (HeatSummaryTable and PhaseScoreTable), leaving EventTitleModal and the lower grid untouched. The plan's approach should follow from that: strip the per-surface hardcoded styling out of the shared Cards so each renders correctly under whichever ThemeProvider wraps it, move that styling into arenaTheme/overlayTheme, and remove the arenaPanelSx workaround — with concrete file-level steps and a way to verify both the arena and the overlay still render. Plan file has a short Grounding section, a plain Before diagram, an After diagram marking what changes, and normal implementation steps.
expectations: The run completes through to a written plan file containing both a Before and an After Mermaid diagram — it does not stall or run out of context during the grounding/investigation step

Grounding is done via reality-check-style parallel investigation subagents across the arena screen, the broadcast overlay, and the shared Card components, and the comparison (an ungraded 'your model' diagram plus a graded reality diagram) is shown to the user before the plan file is written

Grounding surfaces that the per-surface MUI theme split already exists and is wired up (arenaTheme/darkTheme wrapping the arena, overlayTheme/lightTheme wrapping the overlay, each via its own ThemeProvider), so introducing theme wrappers is not the fix

Grounding surfaces that the shared broadcast/Cards components are still styled rather than unstyled — they carry hardcoded styling (e.g. HeatSummaryTable forcing a transparent background in its own sx, BasicBroadcastTable hardcoding cell border and text colours) that overrides the wrapping theme and suits the overlay case, not the arena
